# Render2D Core Profile 1: the normative specification

Specification hash: `7444768605c70c2d19802035ed46da2e74a13a6e7d39b4a823bfe2e1cbc2aedd`

The feature LIST is [`gen/render2d/profile-1.md`](gen/render2d/profile-1.md), which names every entry
the profile carries. This document says what each of them MEANS numerically. Two implementations that
agree on the list and not on the numbers produce different pixels from the same draw list, which is
what a conformance suite exists to catch and what this document exists to prevent.

Everything below composites PREMULTIPLIED and LINEAR, in the canonical intermediate named by
[`IMAGE_COLOR_PROFILE_1.md`](IMAGE_COLOR_PROFILE_1.md). Compositing in an encoded space makes a
half-transparent black edge look grey instead of dark, and it is invisible until two implementations
are compared side by side.

## Compositing operators

The factors ARE the operator:

```text
co = as*Fa*Cs + ab*Fb*Cb ; ao = as*Fa + ab*Fb, with colours premultiplied and linear
```

| operator | Fa, on the source | Fb, on the backdrop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Clear` | `0` | `0` |
| `Src` | `1` | `0` |
| `Dst` | `0` | `1` |
| `SrcOver` | `1` | `1 - as` |
| `DstOver` | `1 - ab` | `1` |
| `SrcIn` | `ab` | `0` |
| `DstIn` | `0` | `as` |
| `SrcOut` | `1 - ab` | `0` |
| `DstOut` | `0` | `1 - as` |
| `SrcAtop` | `ab` | `1 - as` |
| `DstAtop` | `1 - ab` | `as` |
| `Xor` | `1 - ab` | `1 - as` |
| `Plus` | `1` | `1` |

`Plus` is not one of Porter and Duff's twelve and is here anyway: additive light is what a glow, a
highlight and an emissive overlay are, and an implementation without it grows a private one.

## Separable blend modes

`B(Cb, Cs)`, per channel, on UNPREMULTIPLIED values in `0..=1`.

| mode | equation |
| --- | --- |
| `Normal` | `Cs` |
| `Multiply` | `Cb * Cs` |
| `Screen` | `Cb + Cs - Cb * Cs` |
| `Overlay` | `HardLight(Cs, Cb): the operands swapped` |
| `Darken` | `min(Cb, Cs)` |
| `Lighten` | `max(Cb, Cs)` |
| `ColorDodge` | `Cb == 0 -> 0 ; Cs == 1 -> 1 ; otherwise min(1, Cb / (1 - Cs))` |
| `ColorBurn` | `Cb == 1 -> 1 ; Cs == 0 -> 0 ; otherwise 1 - min(1, (1 - Cb) / Cs)` |
| `HardLight` | `Cs <= 0.5 -> Multiply(Cb, 2*Cs) ; otherwise Screen(Cb, 2*Cs - 1)` |
| `SoftLight` | `Cs <= 0.5 -> Cb - (1 - 2*Cs) * Cb * (1 - Cb) ; otherwise Cb + (2*Cs - 1) * (D(Cb) - Cb), where D(Cb) = Cb <= 0.25 ? ((16*Cb - 12) * Cb + 4) * Cb : sqrt(Cb)` |
| `Difference` | `abs(Cb - Cs)` |
| `Exclusion` | `Cb + Cs - 2 * Cb * Cs` |

The two with a division have their ENDPOINTS stated rather than left to whatever the division
produces, and `SoftLight`'s `D(Cb)` is a piecewise function of the BACKDROP with its threshold on
the backdrop - which is the part that is got wrong.

## Non-separable blend modes

These mix the channels, so they need a colour model that the mode's name does not imply.

| mode | equation |
| --- | --- |
| `Hue` | `SetLum(SetSat(Cs, Sat(Cb)), Lum(Cb))` |
| `Saturation` | `SetLum(SetSat(Cb, Sat(Cs)), Lum(Cb))` |
| `Color` | `SetLum(Cs, Lum(Cb))` |
| `Luminosity` | `SetLum(Cb, Lum(Cs))` |

```text
Lum(C)        = 0.3*R + 0.59*G + 0.11*B
Sat(C)        = max(R, G, B) - min(R, G, B)
SetLum(C, l)  = add l - Lum(C) to every channel, then ClipColor
SetSat(C, s)  = order the channels; the smallest becomes 0, the largest s, the middle (Cmid - Cmin) * s / (Cmax - Cmin); if Cmax == Cmin every channel becomes 0
ClipColor(C)  = with l = Lum(C), n = min channel and x = max channel: if n < 0, C = l + (C - l) * l / (l - n); if x > 1, C = l + (C - l) * (1 - l) / (x - l). Luminance is preserved and the chroma is reduced
```

`Lum`'s coefficients are the compositing specification's own fixed triple and stay fixed in every
colour space. That looks wrong and is right: using the destination space's luminance would make
`Luminosity` produce a different result for the same two colours depending on which space they were
tagged with, and the mode is defined as an operation on the numbers rather than on the light.

`ClipColor` is the step every implementation that omits it gets wrong on saturated colours: it
preserves luminance and reduces chroma, rather than clamping each channel.

## Subpixel text

The five-tap FIR across the subpixel triple is `[1, 2, 3, 2, 1] / 9`. Without a filter, subpixel coverage
produces coloured fringes on every stem; with a different filter it produces different fringes.

Coverage is blended through gamma 2.2. Blending it linearly makes light-on-dark text look bolder
than dark-on-light at the same weight, which is the artefact that gets reported as "the font renders
too thin" - and it is a gamma question rather than a font question.

## Geometry

| quantity | value |
| --- | --- |
| flattening tolerance | 0.25 PHYSICAL pixels |
| maximum subdivision depth | 16 |
| at the depth limit | the remaining segment is emitted as a line; the primitive is not refused |
| projective `w` epsilon | 0.00000095367431640625 |
| the horizon rule | clip the segment against w = epsilon in homogeneous space before dividing; a segment entirely beyond it is dropped, and the primitive is refused only if nothing survives |
| point coincidence | 0.00390625 pixels |

ONE tolerance, shared by fills, strokes, boolean operations, hit tests and bounds. If each flattened
to its own, a point would be inside a path for a hit test and outside it for the fill that drew it.
PHYSICAL pixels and not logical ones, because flattening in logical pixels makes a curve on a
two-times display twice as coarse as the same curve on a one-times display - visible as facets on
exactly the screens that show them best.

The coincidence epsilon is a SEPARATE and smaller number: the tolerance is how far a curve may
deviate from its flattening, and this is when two vertices are one. Using the tolerance for both
merges vertices a quarter of a pixel apart, which collapses thin features that were meant to be
there.

## Boolean operations: the answers

Two backends produce different unions if any of these is left open, and the difference is not
subtle: it is a hole that is there in one and not the other.

| question | answer |
| --- | --- |
| how self-intersections are resolved | each operand is rewritten FIRST into non-self-intersecting contours under its own fill rule; operating on a self-intersecting operand makes the result depend on the algorithm's traversal order |
| what an OPEN subpath means as an operand | it is closed with a straight segment from its last point to its first. A boolean operation is defined on REGIONS and an open subpath is not one - and refusing it would fail the commonest use, the union of two stroke outlines |
| how two operands with different fill rules combine | each is resolved to regions under ITS OWN rule first, so the operation is on regions and the two rules never have to agree. The result is non-zero |
| whether the result preserves curves or is polygonised | POLYGONISED at the flattening tolerance, and the profile says so: preserving curves needs exact curve-curve intersection, whose answer is approximate anyway - so the honest form is the polygon, at a tolerance the caller knows |
| the tolerance used | the one flattening tolerance, with points within a coincidence epsilon of each other treated as one |
| the canonical ordering and winding of the output contours | contours sorted by their bounding box's minimum y then minimum x then their first point; an outer contour is wound so its signed area is POSITIVE in the device's y-down space and a hole negative |
| what happens to degenerate and zero-length edges | dropped before the operation. A contour left with fewer than three distinct points contributes nothing, and a result with no contours is an EMPTY path rather than a refusal |
| determinism | the output is a function of the input bytes and the tolerance alone: no reduction whose order depends on threading, and no iteration over a container whose order is not stated |

## Filter graphs: the per-node contract

| rule | value |
| --- | --- |
| shape | a directed acyclic graph; a cycle is refused during preparation |
| bounds map | each node maps an output rectangle to the input rectangle it needs, and produces no pixel outside its declared output |
| working format | the canonical premultiplied linear intermediate, for every node |
| edge mode | transparent black, unless the node states another and the graph records which |
| scratch | computed for the whole graph during preparation, and refused up front |

Without the bounds map the whole graph has to be computed over the whole surface, because nothing can
say which part of the input a part of the output depends on - which is why a blur over a small dirty
region costs a full-screen blur in implementations that skipped it.

## Prepared lists

A prepared list is a CACHE, and a cache whose validity conditions are not enumerated eventually
replays a drawing that is not the one recorded. `is_compatible` checks these and nothing else.

| dependency | why a change invalidates |
| --- | --- |
| profile version and hash | a list prepared against a different profile may contain a command this one does not have, or the same command with a different meaning |
| backend identity and version | the scratch layout and the prepared form are the backend's own; another backend's bytes are not a prepared list, they are bytes |
| target format | quantisation, dithering and the final conversion are all chosen for the target's own format |
| target colour space | every paint was converted into the target's space during preparation |
| physical extent and scale | curves were flattened in DEVICE space, so a different scale is a different flattening |
| immutable resource identity and layout generation | a replaced path, gradient or immutable image is a different drawing under the same index |
| glyph-cache generation | a rasterised glyph the list refers to may have been evicted or re-rasterised at another size |
| filter parameters | a filter's radius decides the scratch reserved for it, which was reserved during preparation |

On a mismatch: a typed re-prepare requirement naming the dependency that changed. Never a silent re-prepare - a caller replaying a list sixty times a
second and getting a full preparation each time has a performance bug it cannot see.

CONTENT IS NOT STRUCTURE: a new frame in a mutable image refreshes that image's upload and sampling cache alone; paths are not re-flattened, scratch is not re-reserved, and the prepared list stays valid.

## The reusable builder

| rule | value |
| --- | --- |
| re-recording within the reservation | no allocation |
| exceeding it | a typed limit or reservation outcome, returned before any replay begins |
| snapshots | one mutated or replaced at a time; a live prepared snapshot retains its own resources |
| scratch on re-preparation | reuse the reservation when it suffices; report the larger requirement explicitly when it does not |

A transform, an opacity, a colour, a scroll offset and an image frame are what an animation changes
between frames; a builder that allocated for any of them would allocate sixty times a second forever.

## Guaranteed minima

A backend may raise any of them; none may be lowered. Without them "supports Profile 1" can mean
"accepts ten path points".

| limit | what it bounds | minimum |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `max_commands` | commands in one list | 65536 |
| `max_resources` | distinct resources | 4096 |
| `max_path_verbs` | path verbs | 65536 |
| `max_path_points` | path points | 262144 |
| `max_subpaths` | subpaths | 8192 |
| `max_clip_depth` | clip depth | 32 |
| `max_layer_depth` | layer depth | 16 |
| `max_filter_nodes` | filter nodes | 64 |
| `max_filter_radius` | filter radius, device pixels | 256 |
| `max_glyphs_per_run` | glyphs per run | 4096 |
| `max_image_extent` | image extent | 16384 |
| `max_layer_pixels` | layer pixels | 67108864 |
| `max_prepared_scratch_bytes` | prepared scratch bytes | 67108864 |
| `max_cache_bytes` | cache bytes | 268435456 |
| `max_display_list_bytes` | display-list bytes | 33554432 |

## Conformance thresholds

A suite without stated tolerances either demands bit-exactness, which no two implementations of a
sine achieve, or demands nothing. Both are ways of not checking. No tolerance may be loosened per
architecture.

| what is compared | tolerance | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| antialiasing coverage | <= 2/255 absolute per pixel against the analytic area, and <= 1/255 mean over the covered region | the per-pixel bound admits one rounding step of an 8-bit coverage value; the mean bound is what stops a systematic bias passing because every pixel is within one step of it |
| a filter kernel's output | <= 1e-3 relative against the kernel evaluated at f64, per channel in linear space | a separable blur is a sum of hundreds of taps, and f32 accumulation over that many terms is worth a thousandth |
| the image comparison mask | EVERY pixel of the target is compared. There is no border exclusion and no mask, and a suite that needs one has found a defect rather than an edge case | an excluded border is where clipping, coverage and the edge rule all fail at once |
| the edge policy | a pixel whose analytic coverage is exactly 0 or exactly 1 is compared EXACTLY; only partially covered pixels carry the coverage tolerance above | a fully covered pixel that differs at all is a colour error wearing an antialiasing tolerance |
